Seymour and octo

seymour-octo.Rmd

Seymour is an L1 larva reconstructed in CATMAID; octo is a second L1 larva in CAVE. octor includes a registration between the two, so neurons can be compared directly.

Using the registration

The registration file (seymour_octo_reg.rds, about 60 MB) is shared separately. Point octor to it once, e.g. in ~/.Rprofile:

options(octor.seymour_reg = "/path/to/seymour_octo_reg.rds")

Then:

library(octor)
library(catmaid)
conn <- catmaid_login(server = "...", token = "...")

nl <- read_seymour_neurons("annotation:^MBON$", conn = conn)
nl_octo <- seymour2octo(nl)            # skeletons and connectors

meshes <- octo_read_meshes(octo_find_ids("^MBON"))
rgl::plot3d(meshes, alpha = 0.3)
rgl::plot3d(nl_octo, col = "red")

seymour2octo() and octo2seymour() work on neurons, neuronlists, meshes and point matrices. All coordinates are in nm. Spelunker shows octo in 8 nm voxels; convert with octo_nm2voxel() and octo_voxel2nm().

How the registration was made

  1. Landmarks: 30 corresponding points (midline points of every VNC segment and mushroom body landmarks on both sides) give an affine transform. Octo is about 1.4 times larger than Seymour in x and y and 1.2 times in z; there is no mirroring.
  2. Synapse clouds: a smooth non-rigid warp then pulls Seymour’s presynaptic connectors onto octo’s synapse predictions (synapses_v8), coarse to fine, while the landmarks are kept in place.
Method Mean error on held-out landmarks
Landmark affine only 5.2 µm
Affine + synapse clouds only 4.6 µm
Landmarks + synapse clouds 3.6 µm

Errors were measured by 5-fold cross-validation over the landmarks.

The weakest region is the posterior VNC. Seymour’s connectors there are sparse, and the only landmarks are on the midline. Adding lateral landmarks there and in the brain outside the mushroom body is the easiest way to improve it.

Refitting 

lm  <- read_seymour_octo_landmarks("seymour_octo_reg.csv")
syn <- octo_synapse_positions()                       # resumable download
con <- seymour_connectors("annotation:^all_somas$", conn = conn)

reg <- fit_seymour_octo_reg(
  lm,
  syn[, c("pre_pt_position_x", "pre_pt_position_y", "pre_pt_position_z")],
  con[, c("x", "y", "z")],
  cv_folds = 5)
reg
saveRDS(reg, "seymour_octo_reg.rds")

The landmark sheet needs the columns include, seymour_loc and octo_loc (nm, "x, y, z"). Only rows with include set to TRUE are used.
